Mr. Taimur Alam Khandaker, Advocate------ for the appellants

full_judgment:
Mr. Khondokar Musa Khaled. J :- This First Misc. Appeal under section 43 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instant of the plaintiffs is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.4.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.806 of 2009 rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

 2. In connection with the aforesaid Misc. Appeal, a Rule was issued on an application for temporary injunction, calling upon the respondent nos.1-6 to show cause as to why they should not be restrained from entering into the office of the Executive Committee of the Co-operative Society and disturbing appellants, in normal activities as the elected members of the said Executive Committee and also dissolving the plaintiff's Executive Committee till 10.8.11, the last date of their three years tenure. 

 5. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of the First Misc. Appeal and connected rule, in short, are that the plaintiff-appellants instituted Title Suit No.806 of 2009 against the defendants-respondents for having declaration that they being elected members of the Ariahazar Upazila Central Co-operative Society, Narayangonj have right to hold office for their elected tenure of three years from 8.7.2008 to 10.8.2011. The election was held on 7.8.2008 and the plaintiff nos.1-2 was elected President and Vice-President of the said Executive Committee respectively while other plaintiffs were elected members. On 12.11.2009 the defendants in collusion with they political party in power, had been trying to procure resignation letters from the plaintiffs' Committee members by putting pressure on them and also dissolve the elected Committee of the said Co-operative Society illegally. Since the defendants had been trying to disturb of the normal function of the plaintiffs as members of the Executive Committee, they field an application for temporary injunction in the said suit for declaration. 

 6. The defendant Nos.1-5 opposed the prayer for temporary injunction by fling a written objection contending inter alia that the defendants having lawful authority to look after the illegal activities perpetrated by the members of the Committee in conducting function of the Committee. Since they voluntarily tendered resignation on 12.11.2009, arrangement had to be made to form Adhoc Executive Committee in accordance with the Rules and procedure of 4 the Co-operative Society. Accordingly, 7 members Adhoc Committee were constituted by the defendants. So the plaintiffs having no locus-standi are not in position to get any order of injunction. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the plaintiffs preferred the instant First Misc. Appeal and obtained the Rule and ad-interim restraining order in the connected Civil Rule. 

 9. Mr. Taimur Alam Khandakar, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants submits that the learned Judge of the trial Court most illegally  rejected the application for temporary injunction without having any reasonable basis in his findings. He submits that when the plaintiffs, being elected members of the Executive Committee, themselves filed the suit to protect their memberships and prayed for temporary injunction, they can not be said to have tendered resignation as decided by the Court below. It is further submitted that out of the 12 members of the Executive Committee, 4 were nominated from amongst the Government officials who were not in a position to resign unless they resign from the Government service. But without proper verification as to the genuineness of the alleged fact of tendering resignation by the plaintiff's, the learned Judge of the trial Court abruptly accepted the contention of the defendants in a very arbitrary and motivated manner. So apparently, the learned Judge of the trial Court committed gross illegality by rejecting the application for temporary injunction and as such the impugned judgment and order is a liable to be set aside. 

 10. Mr. Zaman Akhter, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submits in reply that the First Misc. Appeal and the connected Rule and ad-interim injunction order have become in fructuous in view of the fact that the plaintiffs were elected only for a period of 3 years. Election was held on 7.8.2008 and on obtaining an order of injunction from this Court, they completed their fixed term of office on 7.8.11. So, the plaintiff-appellants having no legal status, cannot now maintain .the appeal and the suit as well. The learned Advocate submits that formation of the new Executive Committee after expiry of their terms of office is being affected seriously due to the restraining order passed in the Civil Rule; and as such it is necessary to vacate the restraining order for the interest of the Co-operative Society. So far merit is concerned the learned Advocate submits that 11 members of the Executive Committee out of 12 had actually tendered resignation at one stage and as such a new Committed was formed in accordance with law. But they could not work dues to the restraining order of this Court. 

 12. We have gone through the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned trial Judge. The sole ground for rejection of the temporary injunction, petitioner appears to be that since 11 members of the Executive Committee out of the 12 including the plaintiffs resigned from their office, they had no prima-facie and arguable case to get temporary injunction, rather such an order, even if passed, would be in fructuous. It appears that the plaintiffs had strongly denied about tendering resignation by swearing affidavit and they not only filed original suit to get protection of their membership but also filed temporary injunction petition in assertion of their original intention of retaining membership of the Executive Committee. In such a situation, the learned Judge of the Trial Court appears to have passed his sweeping remark in a very undesirable manner and it is certainly unbecoming of a judicial officer. Such a controversial issue of the suit should not have been answered in such a way and made the only basis for rejection of the application for temporary injunction in the manner he passed the impugned judgment and order. The disputed issue regarding the resignation of the plaintiffs from the memberships of the Executive Committee is necessarily a matter to be decided in the suit by taking evidence at the time of holding trial. Due such an abrupt finding by the concerned Judge, the suit of the plaintiffs had become non maintainable and infructuous, which is not legally acceptable. As we do not find any other ground for rejection of injunction prayer, certainly such an order cannot be given affirmation in this appeal. 

 13. Admittedly, the plaintiffs were elected members of the concerned Executive Committee for a term of 3 years and in order to protect their right as elected members of the said Executive Committee they had filed the suit. Ultimately they obtained the rule and injunction order after filling the instant First Misc. Appeal and continued to work as elected members of the Executive Committee till today, though their tenure in office of the Executive Committee had already been expired on 7.8.11. The plaintiffs also prayed for protection; of their right by filling temporary injunction petition. But after expiry of the tenure of the office they cannot have any locus-standi to continue as members of the Executive Committee and as such neither they are in a position to maintain the original suit for declaration nor the instant First Misc. Appeal and connected Rule. It is therefore, immaterial to adjudicate as to whether the plaintiffs had tendered resignation or any such resignation letter was obtained by force by or by resorting forgery as alleged by the plaintiffs. 

 14. When it is admitted position of fact that the tenure of three years, for which the plaintiffs were elected members of the Executive Committee of the Co-operative Society, had already been expired on 7.8.11, the instant First Misc. Appeal along with the Rule has become in factitious and on this ground alone, the First Misc. Appeal is liable to be dismissed and the connected Rule discharged.
